newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua resolves beef dispute with El Salvador.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua resolves beef dispute with El Salvador.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman reversed his decision to close Nicaragua's borders to Salvadoran beef imports on Tuesday after El Salvador agreed to re-open its borders to Nicaraguan beef.

Earlier on Tuesday, Aleman had ordered Nicaraguan border officials to prevent the entry of Salvadoran beef after Nicaraguan exporters complained Nicaraguan beef was being blocked from entering El Salvador.
But after a telephone conversation with Salvadoran President Armando Calderon, Aleman said the two had agreed to open their borders to each others' beef, a Nicaraguan government press release said.
Aleman said Calderon told him the closing of El Salvador's border to Nicaraguan beef was a product of a misunderstanding between the Salvadoran government and its ministry of agriculture.
"I was sure these measures did not come directly from the (Salvadoran) executive, but from some other minister. But thanks to God, everything has been cleared up for both countries," Aleman said.

El Salvador is Nicaragua's largest market for beef accounting for 30 percent of its total exports worth $20 million a year, the president of the Nicaraguan National Cattle Commission, Juan Tijerino, said.
